The U.S. Department of Justice extended the ADA Title II web and mobile accessibility deadlines to April 26, 2027 for covered state and local public entities with populations of 50,000 or more, and April 26, 2028 for smaller entities and special district governments. The story A new platform. More than two decades of experience. For more than two decades, Vision-Aid has worked with persons with visual disabilities to enable independence, education and employment. Ability Bazaar is the next chapter: a new platform able to draw on Vision-Aid's deep experience, trusted relationships and vast network across the United States and India to scale quickly. Meet the Ability Bazaar team The people building Ability Bazaar - across Vision-Aid USA and India, research, and AI development. VF Vijay Francis Advisor, Vision-Aid India Vijay is a technology leader with over 25 years in IT and a strong focus on technology for social impact. As an Advisor at Vision-Aid India, he leads strategic initiatives in digital accessibility, AI and assistive technology - empowering persons with visual impairments through accessible digital skills, accessibility engineering and inclusive solutions. Profile for Vijay Francis → VG Vikram Goddla AI Developer Vikram is a rising junior at Harvard University with a strong focus on AI. He has conducted research in artificial intelligence in medicine at Mass General Brigham and Harvard Medical School, including published work on using large language models to improve cancer clinical-trial materials, and brings that AI expertise to the Ability Bazaar platform. She has taught Python and AI to blind students in Uganda, helping make emerging technology more accessible to learners who are often excluded, and hopes to keep expanding access to AI education through inclusive, hands-on learning. HH Harish Hariharan Executive Director, Vision-Aid India Harish is the Executive Director and head of Vision-Aid India. He brings over three decades of leadership across Microsoft, AWS, IBM and other leading technology companies, as well as the nonprofit sector - spanning sales and business development, partnerships, programs and operations, digital skilling, and livelihood creation for persons with disabilities. In 2019 Harvard honored him with the Derek Bok Public Service Award. His research spans algorithms, high-dimensional geometry and the foundations of machine learning. He has volunteered with Vision-Aid since 2005. His career interests center on building scalable AI applications with real impact in healthcare and clinical contexts - expertise he brings to the Ability Bazaar platform. A Arunkumar Technical Lead, Vision-Aid Advanced Technology Center Arunkumar is a Technical Lead at Vision-Aid with over eight years of experience building AI-based solutions to real-world problems, spanning full-stack development, DevOps and mentoring aspiring AI engineers. Arunkumar leads the Vision-Aid Advanced Technology Center team, which designs and builds AI solutions for internal process automation and for external clients - driving efficiency, innovation and measurable impact. Beyond that work sits a deep commitment to the empowerment of visually challenged individuals, and to aligning technical skill with initiatives that create meaningful, accessible impact for that community. The proposition Ability Bazaar is a global, accessibility-first marketplace where persons with disabilities and mixed creator teams use AI App Builder Agents to translate lived-experience problems into practical AI mini-apps. Each tool is delivered through a common accessible shell, validated by PwD users, and made available to individuals, institutions and employers. Vision-Aid's SEP AI Tutor serves as the anchor offering; the long-term scale engine is a trusted creator economy. New platform, proven foundation Ability Bazaar came online in July 2026, but it did not start from zero. Vision-Aid brings more than twenty years of listening to, learning from and delivering programs with persons with visual disabilities. That experience—and a broad network of learners, graduates, accessibility professionals, volunteers, educators, institutions and partners—gives Ability Bazaar the reach and practical knowledge to grow responsibly and quickly. It rolls in DATTC Our Digital Accessibility Testing and Training Center has sold accessibility testing for years - real customers, real revenue, real PwD professionals. Ability Bazaar becomes its storefront, and DATTC becomes the bazaar's proven services engine. It rolls in the AI Development Center Our newest initiative has already shipped the SEP AI Tutor and built Arohi and Nidra. Ability Bazaar becomes the front end to distribute and monetize these apps - and every app that follows. Accountable, by design A marketplace is judged on proof, not promises. Ability Bazaar captures evidence from day one - orders delivered, revenue earned, wages paid to experts with disabilities, and accessibility issues fixed. Honest framing We publish what we measure. Ability Bazaar is worth building in its own right: it aligns with what Vision-Aid already does, and extends it - turning lived experience into livelihood. The roadmap Today : Two engines already running DATTC has delivered paid digital accessibility testing for years, with an established customer base and an AI testing tool co-built with Georgia Tech. The AI Development Center has shipped the SEP AI Tutor and the Arohi and Nidra apps. Phase 1 : One accessible storefront Roll DATTC and the app portfolio into a single Ability Bazaar front end - this platform - so anyone can buy accessibility services or pilot an app from one place. Phase 2 : Marketplace MVP Creator onboarding, the AI App Builder, PwD validation workflow, analytics, institutional access and evidence logs - plus 3-5 new mini-apps in the launch catalogue. Phase 3 : Scaling the commercial backbone Ability Bazaar is open for business today, operated by Vision-Aid. As order volume grows, we are putting in place the operating structure to scale contracts, commerce and creator payouts across the US and India. Phase 4 : Open marketplace Approved creators publish free or paid tools and earn revenue share - a durable marketplace with real users, real revenue and AI-native operations. Nonprofit ownership A Vision-Aid program on its own domain Ability Bazaar and abilitybazaar.com are owned and operated by Vision-Aid, Inc., a United States 501(c)(3) public charity. The separate domain gives this disability-led technology program a clear, accessible home; it is not a separate company or unrelated commercial business. Ability Bazaar directly advances Vision-Aid's charitable mission. It combines training, accessible technology and livelihood creation so people with disabilities can participate as learners, creators, accessibility experts and paid professionals. Revenue from its mission-related services supports delivery, training and paid work within that program.
